## Well-balanced $x_1$ reconstruction: perturbations about a hydrostatic reference (gravity on) {#sec-ch05-wbx1}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Reconstructs $p-p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ along $x_1$ instead of $p$ and
$\rho$, then adds the reference face values back, so a discretely hydrostatic column produces no $x_1$ force.
**Switch.** None. On whenever $g_1\neq0$, the state has a pressure row and the EOS is not `shallow-water`; also
under an $x_1$ block split.
**Requires.** The reference kernel (@sec-ch05-refkernel).
**Order.** Exact rest balance; the face states keep the order of the reconstruction.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-wbx1-split.
:::

A column in hydrostatic balance has pressure and density that fall by orders of magnitude along $x_1$. A high-order
reconstruction of $p$ itself returns face values whose difference across a cell is not exactly $\rho g_1\Delta x_1$,
so a resting column feels a spurious vertical force of the size of the reconstruction error and starts to move.
snapy removes that force by construction: it builds, on every call, a reference $(p_{\mathrm{ref}},
\rho_{\mathrm{ref}})$ whose face pressures satisfy the discrete hydrostatic balance exactly, reconstructs only the
perturbations about it, and restores the reference at the faces. The perturbation of a resting column is a constant,
which every reconstruction reproduces, so the restored faces carry exactly the balanced pressure difference.

The scheme has no switch and no default to change: it is the $x_1$ path whenever gravity acts in $x_1$. The
perturbation ghosts at a physical, non-outflow $x_1$ wall are filled with even parity; the reconstruction runs with
its density and pressure floors off; and a face value that comes out non-positive falls back to the reference
pressure or to the density of the adjacent cell. The $x_2$ and $x_3$ sweeps have no such treatment.

*Aliases.* "WB" or "well-balanced reconstruction" in comments and commit messages; the "base" reference of
`docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §1.

### Derivation

Units: $p$ [Pa], $\rho$ [kg m$^{-3}$], $g_1$ [m s$^{-2}$], $x_1$ and $\Delta x_1$ [m]. This layer uses cell averages
and face point values; a cell average carries an overbar only where a point value of the same quantity appears.

The $x_1$ momentum equation with constant gravity is $\partial_t(\rho v_1)+\partial_1(\rho v_1^2+p)=\rho g_1$.
Integrated over cell $i$ of a Cartesian column, with $p^{*}_{i\pm1/2}$ the face pressures of the Riemann solver,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\overline{\rho v_1})_i = -\frac{\Delta_i[\rho v_1^2+p^{*}]}{\Delta x_1} + \overline{\rho}_i g_1 .
$$

At rest the advective part vanishes and the cell stays at rest exactly when
$p^{*}_{i+1/2}-p^{*}_{i-1/2}=g_1\overline{\rho}_i\Delta x_1$. The reference kernel (@sec-ch05-refkernel) builds face
pressures $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ that satisfy this difference identically, @eq-ch05-refkernel-scan, together with a cell
pressure $p_{\mathrm{ref},i}$, a cell density $\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i}$ and a face density $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$. The
reconstruction then works on the perturbations and restores the reference at the faces:

$$
\begin{aligned}
p'_i &= \overline{p}_i - p_{\mathrm{ref},i}, \\
\rho'_i &= \overline{\rho}_i - \rho_{\mathrm{ref},i}, \\
p^{L,R}_{i-1/2} &= \mathcal R^{L,R}[p']_{i-1/2} + p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2}, \\
\rho^{L,R}_{i-1/2} &= \mathcal R^{L,R}[\rho']_{i-1/2} + \rho_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbx1-split}

with $\mathcal R^{L,R}$ the left and right face values of the configured $x_1$ reconstruction. The subtraction in
@eq-ch05-wbx1-split is done by `_hydro_ref_x1` and the two in-place updates that follow it
([`hydro_forward.cpp:288-293`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L288-L293)),
and the restore by `psf_lo` added back to both states
([`hydro_forward.cpp:357-363`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L357-L363)).

Suppose now that $p'_i=c$ in every cell, for one constant $c$, and $v_1=0$. Every reconstruction of snapy returns a
constant exactly, so $p^{L}=p^{R}=p_{\mathrm{sf}}+c$ at every face, the two states agree, and the Riemann solver
returns $p^{*}=p_{\mathrm{sf}}+c$ with zero mass and energy flux. The momentum balance above then reads
$-(p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2}-p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2})/\Delta x_1+\overline{\rho}_ig_1=0$ by @eq-ch05-refkernel-scan. The
discrete rest state of the scheme is therefore

$$
\overline{p}_i = p_{\mathrm{ref},i}(\overline{p},\overline{\rho}) + c \quad\text{in every cell},
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbx1-rest}

whatever the density reference is: with $v_1=0$ the face density enters no flux. Because $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is rebuilt
from the state, @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest is a fixed-point condition on the column, which `balance_column` solves
(@sec-ch05-balcol). On spherical-polar grids the face areas and the geometric pressure source enter the same
cancellation; the plain-mean form is @sec-ch05-x1cent. The derivation follows
`docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §§1, 6.

*Exact and truncated.* The rest balance is exact for any column satisfying @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest. Away from rest the
face states carry the reconstruction's truncation error on the perturbation plus the offset
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}-\mathcal R[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]$ of the density reference, which is $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ for the
default reference (`[C14]`) and $O(\Delta x_1^4)$ with @sec-ch05-wbref4. The identity used in the cancellation,
that the hydrostatic correction and the pressure force cancel at rest, is `[C19]`.

### Numerical method

Where things live: $\overline p$, $\overline\rho$ and the perturbations are cell averages; $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ and
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ are face point values at the lower face of each cell; the reconstructed states are face
values. The scheme runs in every RK stage, in the $x_1$ block of `HydroImpl::forward`, explicitly.

**Ghosts.** At a physical $x_1$ wall whose boundary function is not an outflow, the $n_g$ ghost cells of $p'$ and
$\rho'$ are overwritten with the mirror image of the first $n_g$ interior cells, even parity, while the velocity keeps
the odd ghosts of the reflecting boundary (@fig-ch05-wbx1-ghosts). A resting perturbation ($p'=c$) is then constant
across the wall too. At an $x_1$ seam the ghosts are the neighbour's cells and the reference is made continuous by
@sec-ch05-seam; at an outflow boundary the ghosts are left as the boundary function wrote them.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-wbx1-ghosts
#| fig-cap: "Perturbation ghosts at a reflecting x1 wall (thick black line), x1 increasing to the right. Top row: the perturbations p' and rho' (sky-blue circles) in three interior cells are mirrored with even parity into the three hatched reddish-purple ghost cells. Bottom row: the normal velocity (black arrows) is mirrored with odd parity. A constant perturbation stays constant across the wall, so a resting column sees no wall force."
#| fig-alt: "Two rows of cells with a thick wall line between three hatched ghost cells on the left and three interior cells on the right; circles mirrored at equal heights in the top row, arrows mirrored with reversed direction in the bottom row."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch05.fig_wbx1_ghosts import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Floors.** The reconstruction of the perturbations is called with `floor=false`, because a perturbation is
legitimately negative and the density and pressure floors would clamp it; the passive-species rows are still
clamped at zero when the EOS limiter is on. After the restore, a non-positive face pressure is replaced by
$p_{\mathrm{sf}}$; a non-positive left density at face $i-\tfrac12$ by $\overline\rho_{i-1}$ and a non-positive
right density by $\overline\rho_i$, the cell on the same side. The adjacent cell, and not $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$, is
used because a reference that overestimates the density aloft turns every floor event at a reflecting top wall into
a large spurious impedance. The shift that builds $\overline\rho_{i-1}$ replicates the first cell instead of
wrapping around the column. @sec-ch08 owns the positivity floors in general.

**Order.** In the interior the face states have the order of the reconstruction applied to a smooth perturbation,
plus the density-reference offset above; at rest the result is exact in interior, wall and seam cells alike. A
column that is not at the fixed point @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest has a residual force of the size of
$p'_i-c$, which is what `balance_column` removes.

: Code map of the well-balanced $x_1$ reconstruction. {#tbl-ch05-wbx1-code}

In the $x_1$ block of `HydroImpl::forward`, in step order (code indices `is`, `iu` are the first and last interior
cell, $i_s$ and $i_u$):

1. `wb_x1` is set from the gravity, the number of state rows and the EOS type
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:262-263`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L262-L263)).
2. Under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` on spherical-polar grids the input `wx1` becomes the plain-mean view of
   @sec-ch05-x1cent; otherwise `wx1` is the state itself.
3. `_hydro_ref_x1` returns $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$, $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$, $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$, and the
   two rows of `wx1` are replaced by the perturbations
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:288-293`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L288-L293)).
4. The even-parity ghosts are written where `is_outflow` is false at a physical wall
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:300-312`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L300-L312)).
5. Under `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` the velocity row is corrected before the reconstruction (Chapter 4).
6. `precon1` reconstructs with `floor=false`
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:346-348`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L346-L348)).
7. The rows of `wx1` are restored, `psf_lo` is added to both pressure states with its fallback
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:357-360`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L357-L360)),
   and the density states get `dsf` with the `rho_below` and own-cell fallbacks
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:362-377`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L362-L377)).

No switch is read here and no warning is issued; the setup checks of the reference are in @sec-ch05-refkernel and
@sec-ch05-wbref4.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The $x_2$ and $x_3$ reconstructions have no well-balanced treatment. A column that is hydrostatic in the continuum
but not at the discrete fixed point @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest is not at rest.
:::

1. **No horizontal treatment.** The $x_2$ and $x_3$ sweeps reconstruct the full state
   (`precon23` [`hydro_forward.cpp:549-551`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L549-L551));
   on a curved grid a stratified column is therefore balanced in $x_1$ only.
2. **Floors off for the perturbation, but not for species.** The species clamp at zero still applies under the EOS
   limiter (table above). Not measured as a source of imbalance.
3. **Moist columns.** No reference meets the floor of a moist column in every case; the choice of reference is a
   parked study (chengcli/snapy#275) and there is no YAML key to choose it (chengcli/snapy#281).
4. **Untested combinations.** See the switch coverage matrix of Chapter 12.
